name: Haiku deep value
strategy: Core value exposure (SPY/VTV) with tactical plays on beaten-down software (ADBE/CRM), defensive dividend anchors (JPM/KO), small tech hedges (SQQQ short), crypto capitulation (BTC spot 4%), tactical GLD short, 17% cash for rebalancing.

positions.thesis: S&P 500 core broad-market exposure; baseline market participation with 2% dividend yield and sector diversification hedge.
Vanguard large-cap value ETF; pure value factor exposure emphasizing low P/E and P/B ratios, complement to SPY.

Adobe down ~49% on AI disruption fears; profitable SaaS with strong FCF, recurring revenue, 0.7% yield; trading well below intrinsic value as market fears overstate threat and underestimate AI integration.
Salesforce similarly capitulated on AI concerns; cloud CRM platform positioning benefits from AI, not threatened; trading at depressed multiple to normalized earnings power.
JPMorgan Chase financial anchor; ~12x P/E, 3% dividend yield, fortress balance sheet, strong FCF; trading discount to intrinsic value.
Coca-Cola dividend aristocrat; 3% dividend yield, unmatched brand moat, recession-resistant cash flows, valuation supported by steady FCF and low cost of capital.
Gold down -6.5% in risk-on H1; tactical short hedge given overweight to growth exposure; limits defensive drag on portfolio.
3x inverse Nasdaq; small hedge against tech concentration volatility; caps upside but protects against tail risk if growth corrects sharply.
Bitcoin at -27% H1 showing multi-year capitulation; small conviction play on deep value entry if macro improves; spot only (no leverage) to control risk profile.

outlook: AI disruption fears on ADBE/CRM should gradually ease over H2 2026 as market realizes these platforms are enhanced, not threatened; dividend anchors and value exposure should compound steadily while hedges cap downside; 17% cash provides flexibility to rebalance into weakness.
